search_strategy: Enumeration-first, not search-first: after an initial targeted 'retry' term-search on Mattermost (step 30), the agent switched to dumping the ENTIRE corpus -- every Mattermost channel via the v4 API into /tmp/chat_all.txt (11031 lines, step 32), every BookStack page WITH comments into /tmp/wiki_all.txt (9024 lines, step ~66), and the full IMAP mailbox into /tmp/mail_all.txt (1424 lines, step ~84) -- then grepped those dumps in waves with widening term lists ('waiver|throttle', then 'CONTRACT|TRANSIENT|TERMINAL|verdict|decide(', then for wiki 'jitter|backoff|exhausted|abort|num_api_errors|num_other_errors|num_rate_limit|cooldown|cool down|retry_policy'). This enumeration strategy is why it caught both wiki-page comments that plain BookStack search would have missed for g3.r1 (g3.r1.l5) and both mail threads for g3.r1 (l8, l12) and one for g3.r2 (s4d). It broke down specifically around remaining_cooldown_seconds: the agent twice PLANNED to add 'cooldown' as a grep term (L2534, L2626, L2931) but the term actually executed each time was a narrower list that omitted it or (once, L147 of the raw tool calls) did include it but the terminal-screen snapshot shown to the model was the truncated tail of a `| head -40` pipe that scrolled past the one wiki comment (g3.r2.s1a) and the one chat remark (g3.r2.s1c) that state the fresh-tracker 0.0 default and the three-decimal rounding rule explicitly. No crashed helper scripts; truncation (both `| head -N` and the visible terminal-screen window) is the recurring failure mode, not tooling breakage.
end_reason: Not applicable -- the run completed normally: code merged to main (commit b9e89a9 via PR #737), Gitea Actions green, release deployed and health-checked (transcript L8899). reward=0.7778 reflects two lost hidden-requirement facts (g3.r2.rule, g3.r2.observability), not a run failure.
notable: v9 rewrite check: this run DID encounter konrad's rewritten 14:12 #code-review turn of 2025-06-03 (the g3.r1.l1 thread) -- transcript L3553 shows the exact new wording 'and length does come good on a retry now and then, so dont stop retrying it, it just shouldnt get as many goes as a timeout'. The agent read it correctly (L3584: 'CONTRACT costing two attempts is corroborated') and shipped finish_reason=="length" as a retryable CONTRACT failure costing 2 attempts (ValueError -> CONTRACT per the ticket's own classify_failure table, decide()'s CONTRACT_ATTEMPT_COST=2 per chat), matching the answer key's observability row exactly (attempts_left=3 -> 1, retried; attempts_left=1 -> 0, contract:exhausted). It was never made terminal/non-retryable.

Root cause of both lost facts is the SAME bug: OnlineStatusTracker.throttle_cooldown_until ships as `float | None = field(default=None)` (raw tool-call patch4.py) instead of the spec's `float = 0.0`, so a freshly constructed tracker reads None where every judge checks `== 0.0` directly against the field.

That None choice is directly traceable to one unretracted line inside the g3.r2.h2 herring exchange -- 'no thats its own reset, sets it to none' (transcript L2587) -- which nobody in the corpus ever reversed (only the exchange's overwrite-vs-max claim was reversed); the agent's own planning notes explicitly carried it forward as 'clear-on-success reset' (L5016, L6006) and built a clear_cooldown() helper and __init__ default around it.

The two remarks that would have caught this -- g3.r2.s1a (wiki comment, literal '0.0 on a fresh tracker...nothing else added for the pause') and g3.r2.s1c (chat, '-3.2 ... 4.999999999998 ... clamp at 0.0, round to three decimals') -- were both never surfaced despite search passes that were textually close: a targeted wiki grep including 'cooldown' WAS executed (raw tool call msg 147) but its terminal-screen snapshot was truncated before reaching this comment, and a planned chat grep for 'cooldown' (L2534/L2626/L2931) was never actually executed with that term in the commands the model ran.

remaining_cooldown_seconds ships without round(...,3) (transcript L5638), which would independently break the boundary case in judge_r2_rule's 'remaining' table (508.0009) even if the None-default bug were fixed; the agent only applied rounding where the ticket itself specified it (delay_for's jitter formula, L137).
